rounds.text: Santosh Fine Fab Ltd is exhibiting a powerful structural turnaround in its top-line trajectory, demonstrated by a robust compounded sales growth rate of 17% over the last 5 years [E14]. This medium-term acceleration directly challenges any narrative of terminal stagnation, supported further by recent operational momentum showing that sales are up quarter-over-quarter [E54]. The market capitalisation sits at a modest ₹ 12.2 Cr [E2], providing immense headroom for re-rating as this growth story gains broader recognition. Furthermore, the stock demonstrates underlying strength by trading near the top of its range, sitting 86% of the way up its 52-week spread between a low of 21 and a high of 37 [E4]. Conceded: trailing twelve months compounded sales growth has dipped slightly by -1% [E16], and the 10-year compounded sales growth records a contraction of -6% [E13].

The bull points to a 17% compounded sales growth over 5 years [E14] to claim a structural turnaround, but this medium-term figure masks complete stagnation and decline elsewhere, specifically a 3-year compounded sales growth of 0% [E15] and a trailing twelve months contraction of -1% [E16]. Conceded: sales are up QoQ [E54], but this short-term blip is heavily outweighed by a sharp -20% year-over-year sales decline [E58] alongside decelerating earnings growth [E59]. The bull's reliance on the stock trading at 86% of its 52-week range [E4] ignores the severe underlying financial weakness, highlighted by an abysmal return on equity of 0.01% compared to the sector benchmark of 5.37% [E8]. Furthermore, the return on assets sits at a negative -0.45%, severely lagging the sector benchmark of 1.97% [E7]. Finally, buying into this momentum means paying a rich price-to-book of 2.18x against a sector benchmark of 1.24x [E6], all while receiving a 0.00% dividend yield [E3] for taking on these outsized operational risks.
